messages.subject: Extracting multiple model parameters
messages.body_plain:
Dear team,

I hope all is well. Thank you for a great package - has made my Mplus life so much easier.

I am busy running multiple simulations and I am struggling a bit now since the extractModelParameters function has been deprecated (The MplusAutomation Examples has not been updated to account for this) . I essentially want to extract the unstandardized parameters of multiple K-class models.

Using allOutput <-readModels("my directory path",recursive = TRUE, filefilter = "[34]{1}-class*",what = "parameters") produces a list of 2, but

allOutput <-readModels("D:/surfdrive/PhD work/Models/GBTM_1/GBTM/1",recursive = TRUE, filefilter = "[34]{1}-class*",what = "parameters")$parameters$unstandardized is a NULL list.

Is there a way to extract the relevant parameters, I'm mostly interested in: subset(params, paramHeader=="Means" & LatentClass !="Categorical.Latent.Variables", select=c("LatentClass", "param", "est", "se"))?

Kind regards,

Gavin

messages.subject: Re: Extracting multiple model parameters
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gavin,

Without seeing your outputs files and directory structure, it's hard to understand what is the cause of the NULL list in the second case. That usually occurs if no files are found in the directory. I would encourage you to open an issue on our Github page: https://github.com/michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation/issues and to upload your output files there for examination (I think they may allow a zip archive of the structure).

In terms of extracting relevant parameters, you can certainly do so. If you want to get a single data.frame that has parameters from all models, you might try something like:

allParams <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:length(allOutput), function(m) {
  params <- allOutput[[m]]$parameters$unstandardized
  params$model <- names(allOutput)[m]
  return(params)
}))

library(dplyr)
allParams <- allParams %>% filter(paramHeader=="Means") %>% select(model, LatentClass, param, est, se)

Hope this helps,
Michael
